1-2.word_for_word: navame — in the ninth chapter; payasi udrikte — when the milk boiled over; gatvā gopī — the gopī went to it; atha tat-kṛtam vilokya — then, seeing what He had done; bhāṇḍa-bhaṅga-ādi — the breaking of the vessel and the other acts; kṛṣṇam dāmnā babandha — she bound Kṛṣṇa with a rope; tan-udara-āśritam viśvam dṛṣṭvā — having seen the universe contained in His small belly; vismita-cetasaḥ — while her mind had been astonished; bandhana-dvi-aṅgula-apūrtyā — by the rope's remaining deficient by two fingers when she tried to bind Him; pūrṇatām anvadarśayat — He showed His fullness/completeness; svayam dadhi nirmamantha — she herself churned the yogurt; tadā ca agāyata — at that time she also sang; ca-kāra-anvayaḥ — the word ca ('and') is connected in this way.
1-2.translation: In the ninth chapter, when the milk boiled over, the gopī went to attend to it; then, seeing Kṛṣṇa's breaking of the vessel and His other acts, she bound Him with a rope. Although she had previously seen the universe contained within His small belly and had been astonished, He now showed His completeness through the rope's repeatedly remaining short by two fingers. In verse 1, 'she herself churned the yogurt.' In verse 2, the word 'and' is to be connected so that the sense is: at that time she also sang.

3.word_for_word: sūtra-naddham — bound with a cord; kāñcī-baddham — fastened with a girdle; rajjoḥ ākarṣeṇa śramaḥ yayoḥ — her two arms were wearied by pulling the churning rope; tayoḥ bhujayoḥ calantau kaṅkaṇau — the bracelets moved upon those arms; kuṇḍale ca — and the earrings moved; kabarāt keśa-pāśāt — from the hair-knot; vigalantyaḥ mālatyaḥ — the mālatī flowers were slipping down; yasyāḥ sā — she whose flowers were thus falling.
3.translation: 'Bound with a cord' means fastened with a girdle. Her two arms were wearied from pulling the churning rope, and the bracelets moved upon them; her earrings moved as well. The mālatī flowers were slipping from her hair-knot.

4.word_for_word: pūrva-ślokasya vyākhyā draṣṭavyā — the explanation of the preceding verse should be consulted.
4.translation: The explanation of the preceding verse should be consulted.

5.word_for_word: adhiśrite — placed upon the hearth; cullim āropite — set on the stove; utsicyamāne — boiling over; ati-tāpena udrīyamāne — rising up because of excessive heat.
5.translation: 'Adhiśrite' means placed upon the hearth, set on the stove. 'Utsicyamāne' means boiling over, rising because of excessive heat.

6.word_for_word: dṛṣad-aśmanā — with a small stone, literally a 'son of a stone'; antaraṃ — the interior; gṛha-madhyam — the inner part of the house; gataḥ — having gone; rahaḥ — in seclusion; ekānte — privately; navanītam abhākṣayat — He ate the fresh butter.
6.translation: 'Dṛṣad-aśmanā' means with a small stone, literally a 'son of a stone.' 'Antaram' means the interior of the house. Having gone inside, He ate the fresh butter privately, in seclusion.

7.word_for_word: suśṛtam — thoroughly heated; sutaptam — very hot; dadhi-manthana-sthānam praviśya — entering the place where the yogurt had been churned; bhinnam sandṛśya — seeing it broken; dṛṣṭvā — having seen it.
7.translation: 'Suśṛtam' means thoroughly heated. Entering the place where the yogurt had been churned and seeing the vessel broken, she understood what had happened.

8.word_for_word: ulūkhalāṅghreḥ — of the mortar turned over; parivartitasya ulūkhalasya upari — on top of the overturned mortar; śici — in the hanging sling; śikye — on the suspended pot-holder; cauryeṇa viśaṅkitam — suspicious because of the theft; cañcalam īkṣaṇam yasya — whose glance was restless; tam sutam — that son.
8.translation: He was on top of the overturned mortar, reaching toward the hanging sling. His glance was restless and apprehensive because of the theft; such was the son whom Yaśodā saw.

9.word_for_word: tapasā — by tapas, here concentration; ekāgryeṇa — by one-pointedness; īritam — directed; tad-ākāratām nītam — brought into conformity with His form; ata eva praveṣṭum kṣamam — and thus fit to enter Him; yoginām manaḥ api yam na āpa — even the minds of yogins did not attain Him; athavā — alternatively; anvadhāvat — she merely ran after Him; na tu āpa — but did not yet reach Him; yoginām manaḥ api — even the mind of yogins; yam praveṣṭum na kṣamam — is not capable of entering Him.
9.translation: 'By tapas' means by one-pointed concentration; the yogins' minds are directed and brought into conformity with His form, and thereby made fit to enter Him, yet even such minds do not attain Him. Alternatively, the sentence may be taken simply to mean that Yaśodā ran after Him but had not yet caught Him—Him whom even the minds of yogins are incapable of entering.

10.word_for_word: anvañcamānā — following along; eva kṛṣṇam anugacchantī — continuing to pursue Kṛṣṇa; bṛhatyoḥ calayoḥ śroṇyoḥ bhareṇa ākrāntā — burdened by the weight of her large moving hips; stabdhā gatiḥ yasyāḥ — whose gait was impeded; visraṃsitāt keśa-bandhanāt — from her loosened hair-knot; cyutaiḥ prasūnaiḥ anugatiḥ — followed by the flowers that had fallen; yad vā — or alternatively; javena kampitāt keśa-bandhanāt — from the hair-knot shaken by her speed; puraḥ patitāni prasūnāni — the flowers fell in front; anu bhayam utpādayantī paścāt gatiḥ yasyāḥ — and as she followed them her movement produced the appearance of the flowers fleeing in fear; parāmṛśat — she seized Him.
10.translation: She continued following Kṛṣṇa. Burdened by the weight and movement of her broad hips, her gait was impeded, and flowers falling from her loosened hair-knot seemed to follow behind her. Alternatively, as her speed shook the hair-knot, flowers fell ahead of her and, as she moved after them, they appeared to flee before her in fear. At last she seized Him.

11.word_for_word: añjan-maṣiṇī — whose eye-black was spreading; añjantī sarvataḥ prasarantī maṣī yayoḥ te akṣiṇī — the two eyes around which the collyrium spread in every direction; sva-pāṇinā kaṣantam — rubbing them with His own hand; saṃmardayantam — wiping/rubbing them; bhiṣayantī — frightening Him; hrasvaḥ chāndasaḥ — the shortened form is Vedic/metrical; bhīṣayantī bhayam utpādayantī — causing fear; avāgurat — she threatened/scolded Him; abhartsyayat — she rebuked Him.
11.translation: The collyrium around His eyes was spreading as He rubbed and wiped His eyes with His own hand. 'Bhiṣayantī' is a metrically shortened form of 'bhīṣayantī,' meaning that she frightened Him. 'Avāgurat' means that she threatened and rebuked Him.

12.word_for_word: iyeṣa — she desired; aicchat — she wished; atad-vīrya-kovidā — not knowing His power; tat-prabhāva-anabhijñā — unaware of His majesty.
12.translation: 'Iyeṣa' means 'she desired' or 'she wished.' 'Atad-vīrya-kovidā' means that she did not know His power and was unaware of His majesty.

13-14.word_for_word: akovidatvam āha — he explains her lack of knowledge; na ca antar iti pañcabhiḥ — in the five statements beginning 'there is neither inside'; bandhanam hi — binding ordinarily occurs; bahiḥ-parivṛtena dāmnā — by a rope encircling from outside; antar-āvṛtasya — something enclosed within; pūrva-apara-vibhāgavataḥ vastunaḥ — of an object having front and back divisions; pūrvataḥ dāma dhṛtvā — placing the rope at the front; paritaḥ pariveṣṭanena — and wrapping it around; sambhavati — binding becomes possible; na tu etat asti — but none of this applies to Him; vyāpakena vyāpyasya bandhaḥ bhavati — what pervades can bind what is pervaded; tat ca viparītam — but here the relation is the reverse; tad-vyatiriktasya abhāvāt — because nothing exists apart from Him; na bandhaḥ — binding is impossible; tam martya-liṅgam adhokṣajam — that Adhokṣaja appearing in a mortal form; ātmajam matvā — regarding Him as her own son; babandha — she bound Him.
13-14.translation: Śrīdhara explains Yaśodā's lack of knowledge through the statements beginning 'there is neither inside nor outside.' Binding ordinarily occurs when a rope surrounds from outside something enclosed within. It is possible for an object that has front and back: one places the rope before it and wraps the rope around. None of these conditions applies to Him. Moreover, something larger and pervasive binds what is smaller and pervaded, whereas in His case the relation is reversed; and because nothing exists apart from Him, there is nothing external by which He could be bound. Nevertheless, regarding Adhokṣaja in His mortal-appearing form simply as her own son, Yaśodā bound Him.

15.word_for_word: dvi-aṅguloḥ na — not 'by two fingers' in the instrumental sense; dvābhyām aṅgulābhyām — by two fingers; ūnam — deficient; apūrṇam — incomplete, short.
15.translation: The expression means that the rope was deficient or short by the measure of two fingers; 'ūnam' means incomplete or lacking.

16.word_for_word: pūrva-ślokasya vyākhyā draṣṭavyā — the explanation of the preceding verse should be consulted.
16.translation: The explanation of the preceding verse should be consulted.

17.word_for_word: smitam kurvatīnām madhye — among the gopīs who were smiling; svayam api hasantī — she herself also laughing; vismayam āpa — became astonished.
17.translation: Among the gopīs who were smiling, Yaśodā herself also laughed, yet at the same time she became astonished.

19.word_for_word: na ca evam svātantrya-bhaṅgaḥ — this does not imply a loss of His independence; iti āha — therefore the verse says; evam sandarśitā — thus He displayed; seśvaram idam viśvam — this universe together with its rulers; vaśe — is under control; yad-adhīnam — subject to Him.
19.translation: This display of being controlled by His devotee does not destroy His own independence. The verse therefore says that He 'thus displayed' His subordination to His servant, while this entire universe, together with its rulers, remains under His control and subject to Him.

20.word_for_word: bhagavat-prasādam anye api bhaktāḥ labhante — other devotees also obtain the Lord's grace; idam tu aticitram — but this is exceedingly extraordinary; iti sa-romāñcitam āha — he speaks of it with hair standing on end; viriñcaḥ putraḥ api — Brahmā, although His son; bhavaḥ sva-ātmā api — Śiva, although His very self; śrīḥ jāyā api — Śrī, although His wife.
20.translation: Other devotees also receive the Lord's grace, but this grace received by the gopī is extraordinarily wondrous; Śrīdhara speaks of it as though with hairs standing on end. Brahmā did not obtain it, although he is the Lord's son; Śiva did not, although he is His very self; nor did Śrī, although she is His wife.

21.word_for_word: phalitam āha — he states the conclusion; na ayam iti — with the verse beginning 'this Lord is not easily attained'; dehinām — of those identified with the body; deha-abhimāninām tāpasa-ādīnām — ascetics and others possessing bodily identification; jñāninām — of knowers; nivṛtta-abhimānānām api — even of those whose identification has ceased.
21.translation: He states the conclusion with the verse beginning 'this Lord is not easily attained.' 'Embodied persons' means ascetics and others who remain identified with the body; 'jñānins' means even those whose bodily identification has ceased. Neither attains Him as easily as those endowed with devotion do.

22.word_for_word: bhaktaiḥ baddhasya api — although bound by devotees; anya-mocakatvam — His power to liberate others; āha — he states; kṛṣṇaḥ tu iti — with the verse beginning 'but Kṛṣṇa.'
22.translation: Although He Himself had been bound by His devotee, He still possessed the power to free others. Śuka now states this with the verse beginning 'but Kṛṣṇa.'
